extracted.intended_audience: African short-story writers, publishers, and the literary/literary-prize community
extracted.subtask_description: Announcement and guidance about submissions and judging approach for the 2026 Caine Prize for African Writing, including what the judges are seeking in stories and key logistical details (deadlines, prizes, shortlist).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejecting an essentialised 'Caine Prize/African story' stereotype
rubrics_metrics.description: “We have been intentional about challenging the idea that there is such a thing as a ‘Caine Prize story’ and, by extension, an ‘African story.’”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging panels are assembled to actively challenge fixed expectations about what a winning story should look like; publishers and writers are encouraged to abandon inherited assumptions about an 'ideal' story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Valorising the best short stories being written today
rubrics_metrics.description: Judges are "united by one purpose: valorising the best short stories being written today."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selections aim to highlight contemporary excellence in short fiction rather than conforming to a prescriptive template.

rubrics_metrics.name: Champion boldness of form, perspective, genre, and themes
rubrics_metrics.description: “We champion boldness – of form, perspective, genre, and themes – and we urge writers to push beyond the familiar edges of their practice.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Work that experiments with structure, viewpoint, genre-blending, or thematically daring material is explicitly encouraged.

rubrics_metrics.name: Push beyond the familiar edges of your practice (innovation/experimentation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Prize "urges writers to push beyond the familiar edges of their practice."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider taking creative risks rather than repeating well-worn approaches; judges are looking for evidence of development, risk-taking, or newness in craft.

rubrics_metrics.name: Capacity to surprise
rubrics_metrics.description: The judges are "eagerly waiting for your submissions and the stories that will surprise us all."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unexpectedness—in plot, voice, perspective, or resolution—is valued; stories that subvert expectations or offer fresh angles are likely to stand out.

rubrics_metrics.name: Diversity of voices and viewpoints in shortlist selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The shortlist should "resist expectation and reflect... a ‘kaleidoscope of contemporary African voices.'"
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judging panels are intentionally composed of cultural producers from different disciplines, geographies, generations, and lived experiences to ensure a varied and representative shortlist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission channel: publishers submit work
rubrics_metrics.description: The announcement references submissions coming from publishers: "As publishers continue to submit work..."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions are expected to be routed via publishers (the page implies publishers submit stories for consideration); entrants should ensure compliance with the Prize's submission process (consult official rules for specifics).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for the 2026 Caine Prize close at midnight on 27 February 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All submissions must be received by that deadline to be eligible; late entries will not be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist size and announcement date
rubrics_metrics.description: A shortlist of five stories and authors will be announced on 1 September 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect a five-entry shortlist; plan publicity and availability accordingly if submitted or shortlisted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prizes, translation split, and publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Each shortlisted writer will receive £500, the overall winner will be awarded £10,000, and where a winning story is a translation the prize will be split 70% to the author and 30% to the translator. Shortlisted stories will be published in the official Caine Prize anthology alongside work produced at the Prize’s annual workshop.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Monetary awards and publication opportunities are specified; translators are financially recognised if a translated work wins. Shortlisted authors gain anthology publication as part of the Prize.
